'''Baldwyn Torto''' is a Ghanaian [[chemical ecologist]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Graham|first=Flora|date=2020-07-08|title=Daily briefing: Kill, confuse, eat — how to stop a plague of locusts|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-02067-0|journal=Nature|language=en|doi=10.1038/d41586-020-02067-0|pmid=34234319|s2cid=235768406|access-date=2022-03-02|archive-date=2020-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116091236/https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-02067-0|url-status=live|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and the first natural scientist from [[Ghana]] to be elected as an International Member of the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2023<ref name="nasonline.org">{{cite web | url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/baldwyn-torto-xvqyb4/ | title=Baldwyn Torto – NAS }}</ref> for groundbreaking discoveries in chemical ecology.  His work has opened new pathways for vector control and the monitoring of crop pests and other insects. He is an ARS Distinguished Visiting Scientist, and an Emeritus Fellow at the [[International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology|International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE)]], where he previously served as a principal scientist and head of the Behavioural and Chemical Ecology Unit.<ref>{{Citation|title=Professor Baldwyn Torto, Principal Scientist, ICIPE| date=19 November 2013 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yFiED6nIQTE|language=en|access-date=2022-02-03|archive-date=2016-03-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329171155/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yFiED6nIQTE|url-status=live}}</ref> Additionally, he holds a position as an [[Academic ranks in South Africa#Overview|extraordinary  professor]] in the Department of Zoology and Entomology at the [[University of Pretoria]], South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Baldwyn Torto - Person|url=https://sustainability-innovation.asu.edu/person/|access-date=2022-02-03|website=Global Institute of Sustainability and Innovation|language=en-US}}</ref> He became a fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]] in 2013,<ref name="aasciences.africa">{{cite web | url=https://aasciences.africa/fellows/torto-baldwyn | title=Fellow &#124; the AAS }}</ref> and a fellow of the [[Entomological Society of America]] in 2016.<ref name="entsoc.org">{{cite web | url=https://www.entsoc.org/fellows/torto | title=Baldwyn Torto, ESA Fellow (2016) &#124; Entomological Society of America | date=December 2024 }}</ref> He is a member of the [[American Chemical Society]] and was once a Councilor for the International Society of Chemical Ecology.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.icipe.org/news/icipe%E2%80%99s-prof-baldwyn-torto-appointed-esa-fellow | title=News and Events &#124; icipe - International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Torto was born in [[Accra]] in 1955.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Baldwyn Torto, ESA Fellow (2016)|url=https://www.entsoc.org/fellows/torto|access-date=2022-02-03|website=www.entsoc.org|language=en|archive-date=2021-12-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222211342/https://www.entsoc.org/fellows/torto|url-status=live}}</ref> He obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] with honors degree in Chemistry and Biochemistry from the [[University of Ghana]] in 1979, and master's degree in natural product chemistry under the mentorship of Prof. Ivan Addae-Mensah FGA in 1982 from the same university. In 1985, he was the first African to be trained in chemical ecology at [[ICIPE]] and worked on the chemical basis of sorghum-stem borer interactions under the mentorship of Prof. Ahmed Hassanali FAAS and graduated with a doctorate degree at the [[University of Ghana]] in 1988.<ref name="entsoc.org"/>

== Career and Research ==
Following his postdoctoral research in organic chemistry under the mentorship of Professor Michael D. Bentley and Professor Barbara J.W. Cole at the [[University of Maine]], Torto joined [[International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology|ICIPE]] as a Scientist in 1991.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Hardie|first1=Jim|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xEcgAQAAMAAJ&q=baldwyn+torto|title=Pheromones of Non-lepidopteran Insects Associated with Agricultural Plants|last2=Minks|first2=A. K.|date=1999|publisher=CABI Pub.|isbn=978-0-85199-345-4|language=en}}</ref> In 2000, he became a senior scientist and a Rothamsted International Fellow under the mentorship of Professor John A. Pickett [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], at the Rothamsted Research in the United Kingdom.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Torto Baldwyn {{!}} The AAS|url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/torto-baldwyn|access-date=2022-02-03|website=www.aasciences.africa|archive-date=2019-10-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191020105131/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/torto-baldwyn|url-status=live}}</ref> A year later, he was a visiting scientist under the mentorship of Professor James H. Tumlinson NAS and Dr. Peter E. A. Teal at the [[USDA-ARS|USDA/ARS]]-Centre for Medical, Agriculture and Veterinary Entomology in [[Gainesville, Florida|Gainesville]], Florida.<ref name=":1" /> He worked in this capacity collaborating with colleagues at CMAVE, Professor Drion G. Boucias, University of Florida, and Professor Marla Spivak, University of Minnesota, on the semiochemical management of honey bee pests until 2006. A year later, he returned to [[ICIPE]] as a research leader and principal scientist.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eating stink bugs could boost health in Africa|url=https://www.scidev.net/global/news/stink-bugs-boost-health-nutrition-africa/|access-date=2022-02-03|website=SciDev.Net|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-12-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211219042645/https://www.scidev.net/global/news/stink-bugs-boost-health-nutrition-africa/|url-status=live}}</ref> He was responsible for the Behavioural and Chemical Ecology Unit (BCEU).<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ragaini|first=Richard C.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RcvFCgAAQBAJ&dq=baldwyn+torto&pg=PA695|title=International Seminar On Nuclear War And Planetary Emergencies - 40th Session|date=2009-08-03|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4466-51-6|language=en|access-date=2022-03-02|archive-date=2022-03-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302202215/https://books.google.com.gh/books?id=RcvFCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA695&dq=baldwyn+torto&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjd-YO_0OP1AhVOilwKHQ_2AK4Q6AF6BAgHEAM#v=onepage&q=baldwyn%20torto&f=false|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Hardege|first=Jorg D.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5k-6CwAAQBAJ&dq=baldwyn+torto&pg=PA199|title=Chemical Ecology|date=2009-06-10|publisher=EOLSS Publications|isbn=978-1-84826-179-2|language=en|access-date=2022-03-02|archive-date=2022-03-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302202218/https://books.google.com.gh/books?id=5k-6CwAAQBAJ&pg=PA199&dq=baldwyn+torto&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjd-YO_0OP1AhVOilwKHQ_2AK4Q6AF6BAgFEAM#v=onepage&q=baldwyn%20torto&f=false|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SMg-AQAAIAAJ&q=baldwyn+torto|title=New Scientist|date=2007|publisher=New Science Publications|language=en|access-date=2022-03-02|archive-date=2022-03-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220302202202/https://books.google.com.gh/books?id=SMg-AQAAIAAJ&q=baldwyn+torto&dq=baldwyn+torto&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjd-YO_0OP1AhVOilwKHQ_2AK4Q6AF6BAgEEAM|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Invasive weed could fuel malaria transmission|url=https://www.scidev.net/sub-saharan-africa/news/invasive-weed-could-fuel-malaria-transmission/|access-date=2022-02-03|website=Sub-Saharan Africa|language=en-US|archive-date=2021-08-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210824184913/https://www.scidev.net/sub-saharan-africa/news/invasive-weed-could-fuel-malaria-transmission/|url-status=live}}</ref> Torto works with the University of Pretoria as an [[Academic ranks in South Africa#Overview|extraordinary  Professor]].<ref name=":2"/>
 
Torto is credited for 240 publications, and his works have been cited over 8,000 times.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Loop {{!}} Baldwyn Torto|url=https://loop.frontiersin.org/people/886825/overview|access-date=2022-02-03|website=loop.frontiersin.org|archive-date=2022-01-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120143723/https://loop.frontiersin.org/people/886825/overview|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Baldwyn TORTO {{!}} Principal Scientist and Head of Department {{!}} PhD Organic Chemistry/Chemical Ecology {{!}} icipe – International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology, Nairobi {{!}} ICIPE {{!}} Behavioural and Chemical Ecology, International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Baldwyn-Torto|access-date=2022-02-03|website=ResearchGate|language=en|archive-date=2021-10-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029212852/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Baldwyn-Torto|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=-H_82mMAAAAJ&hl=en | title=Baldwyn Torto }}</ref> His research interests are in the field of chemical ecology application to sustainable agriculture, veterinary, public health and the environment<ref name="web.archive.org">{{cite web | url=http://www.icipe.org/about/staff/baldwyn-torto | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210511134338/http://www.icipe.org/about/staff/baldwyn-torto | archive-date=11 May 2021 | title=Baldwyn Torto &#124; icipe - International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology }}</ref> and has identified semiochemicals for the management of locusts, fruit flies, plant parasitic nematodes, spider mites, legume pests, and invasive species including the south American tomato pinworm and potato cyst nematode. Others include vectors of infectious diseases such as malaria, dengue, Rift Valley Fever, leishmaniasis, and trypanosomosis.    
 
He serves on the editorial committees of the ''[[Annual Review of Entomology]]''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/ento?page=editorial-committee | title=Annual Review of Entomology }}</ref> and ''[[Current Opinion in Insect Science]]''.<ref>https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/current-opinion-in-insect-science/about/editorial-board</ref> Currently, he is Chief Specialty Editor for Vector Biology in ''[[Frontiers in Tropical Diseases]]'',<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/tropical-diseases/sections/vector-biology/editors | title=Frontiers in Tropical Diseases &#124; Vector Biology }}</ref> and Associate Editor for the ''[[Journal of Chemical Ecology]]'' <ref>{{cite web | url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10886/editorial-board | title=Journal of Chemical Ecology }}</ref> and has previously held similar roles for ''[[Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences]]'', and ''[[Pest Management Science]]''. He has also served as an advisory board member of the ''[[Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry]]''.<ref name="web.archive.org"/>

== Honours ==
In 2023, Torto was elected International Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] ([[United States]]);<ref name="nasonline.org"/> in 2016, elected fellow of the [[Entomological Society of America]];<ref name="entsoc.org"/> and in 2013, elected fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="aasciences.africa"/> He was the recipient of the 2020 icipe@50 Achievement Award for his scientific research and immense contribution to the training of the next generation of African scientists, the Nan-Yao Su Award for Innovation and Creativity in Entomology of the [[Entomological Society of America]] in 2019. In 2018, he was awarded the Louis Malassis International Prize for Food and Agriculture for Outstanding Career in Agricultural Development by the Agropolis Foundation in France, and in 2017, he was honoured by the ''[[Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry]]'' (AGRO-division, American Chemical Society) with the Journal Article of the Year prize. That same year, he was named by the [[South African Department of Science and Technology]] as one of the top 50 scientists in Africa.<ref name="web.archive.org"/>

Torto has delivered many plenary and keynote presentations at various conferences, some of these conferences include 75th International Symposium on Crop Protection,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ilvo.vlaanderen.be/nl/agenda/75th-international-symposium-on-crop-protection | title=75th International Symposium on Crop Protection - ILVO Vlaanderen | date=21 May 2024 }}</ref> 13th Arab Congress of Plant Protection,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/00094c40-7626-4947-8966-257155b715ee | title=Abstracts book of the 13th Arab Congress of Plant Protection, Hammamet, Tunisia, 16-21 October 2022 | date=16 October 2022 | last1=Kumari | first1=Safaa | last2=Makkouk | first2=Khaled | last3=Daami-Remadi | first3=Mejda | last4=Najar | first4=Asma | last5=Ben Ghanem | first5=Hajer | last6=Nader | first6=Asaad | last7=Kassem | first7=Mohammad | last8=Moukahel | first8=Abdulrahman }}</ref> International Society of Chemical Ecology, the XXV 2016 International Congress of Entomology, Orlando, Florida,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NGILPtA7bz0 | title=ICE 2016 Plenary Presentation Featuring Dr. Baldwyn Torto | website=[[YouTube]] | date=10 April 2017 }}</ref> 13th Arbovirus and Mosquito Workshop and NE1443 Regional Project Workshop, USA and the General assembly of the African Academy of Sciences.

He served on the Jury of the Falling Walls Foundation Breakthroughs for Life Sciences, Berlin (2022-2024)<ref>https://falling-walls.com/falling-walls-science-summit/science-summit-2025/life-sciences</ref> and he is on the board of trustees of the JRS Biodiversity Foundation and became its president in 2020.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://jrsbiodiversity.org/about-jrs/people/ | title=People }}</ref>  He is a reviewer for research grants for many organizations across the globe.<ref name="entsoc.org"/>

== Personal life ==
Torto is married to Rita, an animal physiologist. Together, they have three sons. His hobbies include cooking, gardening, and playing the guitar.<ref name=":1" />
